steps.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, sugar, cream of tartar and salt. Stir in butter and milk just until moistened. Drop batter on a lightly greased cookie sheet by the tablespoon.
Bake in preheated oven until golden on the edges, about 8 to 12 minutes. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: E-Z Drop Biscuits
raw_recipe.description: Quick and easy drop biscuits that taste great with butter and jam or plain with sausage and gravy.
raw_recipe.name: E-Z Drop Biscuits

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, sugar, cream of tartar and salt. Stir in butter and milk just until moistened. Drop batter on a lightly greased cookie sheet by the tablespoon.
Bake in preheated oven until golden on the edges, about 8 to 12 minutes. Serve warm.

review.reviewBody: I have made these with and without the cream of tartar, and much prefer them without. The cream of tartar, I thought, gave them a slight bitter aftertaste. With that correction, these are tender, fluffy, and ohhh so tasty. Not to mention EASY. Hope that little tip helps everyone.

Excellent easy receipe. Note - Baking Soda already has some Cream of Tarter, or similar acidic leavening in it, and this may be the reason Cream of Tarter may be left out without too noticeable an effect. Also note all dry ingredients should be mixed THROUGHLY before adding liquids.

Finally, note there is a TIME LIMIT of about 15 to 20 minutes from the time you have added liquid to Baking Powder until you start baking them for Baking Power to have its best leavening(rising)affects. So be sure to preheat oven so its ready for baking when bisquits mixed and ready

I replaced tartar with 1 tsp. of white vinegar and added about 2 tblsp. of flour. Baked it for 10 minutes. Tops stayed light but bottoms were golden brown...so check them especially if you use a dark nonstick pan like I did. I will never use bisquick mix again. They were light, fluffy and flavorful. Great basic recipe. Would be lovely with herbs added to mix...nice with poultry or pork dinners.

This is a great recipe, only made a few changes. I did not use cream of tartar and substituted buttermilk for milk and probably used a bit more then a cup. I also grated the butter into the flour instead of melting it. I sprinkled cinnamon and sugar on some, cheddar cheese on some and left some alone. They were delicious and I will definitely be making these again!

So amazing! I use a grater to shred the butter into the dry ingredients and then mix in either dried berries and nuts (breakfast) or garlic and cheese and herbs (savory) before slowly blending in the milk and baking.
My boys LOVE the buttery texture of the nut and berries.
(By the way I suck at baking but can make these all day long! Easy to make!)

Tried the recipe last week with cheese and my kids really enjoyed them! I baked at 400° for 12 minutes as my parchment paper isn’t safe in the oven over 415° . They were delicious. Moist and tender. This is a basic recipe that I think I can do a lot with - or not, depending on my mood!

I made them again yesterday with a tablespoon more sugar, added frozen blueberries and sprinkled with powdered sugar before baking . Also substituted coconut oil for the butter. They were moist and delicious!

Very good. I added one cup of grated cheese, omitted the cream of tartar as recommended by others, and also grated in the frozen butter to make them flaky, as someone suggested. I will make these again, thanks.

The easiest, fluffiest, and lightest drop biscuits I've ever made. I happened to be out of sugar, but it personally didn't matter to me. Couldn't taste a difference without it. Possible b/c I had made them savory. I added a cup of cheddar cheese to the dough before baking and then brushed them all with melted garlic butter when they came out. They were divine. Paired perfectly with my soup.
These were excellent...I grated a stick of frozen butter instead of melting it and they were very flaky...

Like others, I left out the cream of tartar and they were great. We are gluten free and so I used Bob’s Red Mill Gluten Free flour. These are lighter and crispy on the top. Will put into our breakfast / dinner rotation. Thanks!
With 1 tsp granulated garlic and 1/2 c. shredded cheddar, these taste just like the Cheddar Bay Biscuits at Red Lobster.

Incredibly easy recipe to follow. Made the perfect quick biscuits for a last minute soup I forgot to get bread for. I even used almond milk and they were still edible so I know following exact these would be excellent. Thanks for the easy recipe!!
I use this recipe so much! Definitely a prefered family favorite. Most of the time I leave out the sugar and no one notices.
I love this recipe ! So easy, I mean EZ....and yummy❤️
super easy, great flavor.

Used oil instead of melted butter. Left out the tarter. Loved the ease and they were tasty too. Looked like the picture with 12 minutes in the oven. I will add garlic and shredded cheese as suggested by others next time. I expect them to be delicious.
This is my go to recipe for biscuits. My family loves for biscuits and gravy.
Delicious

So easy! We make a double batch and cook it in a cast iron pan like you would corn bread. Fluffy, tender biscuits cut from the "big biscuit." Served with sausage gravy my family begs me to make it. Never any left and we are New Orleans natives where sausage gravy is not a staple.
Super easy and took less time than advertised… simply delightful. We had just made blackberry jam and wanted an easy biscuit .. this was perfect! Thank you! -Cory
